citeAs: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao (2024). Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330.
creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao (University of Science and Technology of China, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai AI Laboratory)
description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans, benchmarking 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes. It is designed to evaluate large vision-language models' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples that exhibit visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and require advanced multi-modal capabilities.
name: MMStar
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: After automated coarse filtering, three experts conducted manual review to ensure: (1) each sample's answer is based on understanding visual content; (2) selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; (3) most samples require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities. Samples were split into four difficulty categories (easy: 12-16 LVLM hits, moderate: 8-11, hard: 4-7, tough: 0-3) to guide selection. Finally, 1,500 high-quality samples were manually curated considering diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
rai:dataBiases: The paper identifies two primary biases in existing benchmarks that MMStar is designed to mitigate: (1) visual content is unnecessary for many samples (answers can be inferred from text alone), and (2) unintentional data leakage exists in LLM and LVLM training. MMStar addresses these by filtering samples where more than 2 of 8 LLMs can answer correctly without visual input.
rai:dataCollection: Samples were first roughly selected from six existing benchmarks (MMMU, MMBench, ScienceQA, AI2D, SEED, MathVista) using an automated pipeline with eight LLM inspectors to filter out visually unnecessary or leaked samples, then manually reviewed by three experts to curate 1,500 high-quality samples.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples sourced from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: MMMU (MMMU-Val), MMBench (MMBench-EN-Dev), ScienceQA (ScienceQA-Test), AI2D (AI2D-Test), SEED (SEED-Image), and MathVista (MathVista-Mini), totaling 22,401 samples before filtering.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that even the best model (GPT-4V high-resolution) scores under 60% on average on MMStar, and the authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set to further reduce accidental data leakage into future LLM and LVLM training corpora.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated coarse filtering pipeline was applied using eight LLM inspectors (two closed-source: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro; six open-source: LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, etc.) with 2-shot in-context inference. Samples answered correctly by more than 2 of the 8 LLMs were excluded. This reduced the pool from 22,401 to 11,607 candidate samples. The 16 LVLMs were then used to gauge difficulty and split samples into four levels (easy, moderate, hard, tough).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to provide a fairer and more accurate evaluation of LVLMs, preventing misjudgments of actual multi-modal gains and avoiding misguiding the research community. It addresses the risk that data leakage and visually unnecessary samples could lead to unfair model comparisons and incorrect conclusions about model capabilities.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating large vision-language models' (LVLMs) multi-modal capabilities across 6 core capability dimensions (Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, Mathematics) and 18 detailed axes. Also used to measure data leakage and actual multi-modal performance gain via the proposed MG and ML metrics.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLM inspectors used for automated filtering: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro (closed-source), LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B (open-source). Additionally, 16 LVLMs (including GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, LLaVA series) were used to gauge sample difficulty.

evidence.rai:dataCollection: We first choose two benchmarks [27, 21] focused on natural images and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge [51, 30, 20, 29] for our sample collection. We then develop an automated pipeline to preliminarily filter out samples that do not meet the first two criteria. Specifically, we employ two closed-source LLMs [41, 34] and six open-source LLMs [1, 42, 49, 3, 19, 43] sizing 20B or larger to serve as inspectors.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: The MMStar is a new benchmark that "Stands on the shoulders of giants". Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline. In detail, we use eight powerful LLMs as candidates inspectors for visual dependency and LLM leakage
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: As illustrated in Figure 4, following this initial coarse filtering, our sample pool was reduced from 22,401 to 11,607.
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: we employ two closed-source LLMs [41, 34] and six open-source LLMs [1, 42, 49, 3, 19, 43] sizing 20B or larger to serve as inspectors. These open-source LLMs are applied with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy to minimize response refusals and ensure consistency in answer formatting. Following this, we evaluate the sample pool with these LLM inspectors, documenting the hit frequency for each evaluation sample. Finally, we only retain those samples with hit counts of two or fewer hits, indicating that around 75% of LLM inspectors fail to provide the correct answer.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: After the coarse filtering with LLM inspectors, we further employ three experts to conduct the manual review process to ensure: 1) each sample's answer should be based on the understanding of visual content; 2) selected samples should cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; 3) most samples should require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: After the coarse filtering with LLM inspectors, we further employ three experts to conduct the manual review process to ensure: 1) each sample's answer should be based on the understanding of visual content; 2) selected samples should cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; 3) most samples should require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution.
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: we use eight powerful LLMs as candidates inspectors for visual dependency and LLM leakage, including two closed-source APIs (GPT4-Turbo [34], and GeminiPro [41]) and six leading open-source models (e.g., LLaMA-70B [43], Qwen-1.5-72B [1], and Mixtral-8x7B [19]). Samples that could be answered by more than 2 of the 8 LLMs are excluded as they may exist leaking or visual-unnecessary problems. Then we use 16 leading LVLMs (e.g., GPT4V [35], GeminiPro-Vision [41], LLaVA series [24, 26]) to gauge the difficulty of the samples and split them to four levels.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: we dig into current evaluation works and identify two primary issues: 1) Visual content is unnecessary for many samples. The answers can be directly inferred from the questions and options, or the world knowledge embedded in LLMs. 2) Unintentional data leakage exists in LLM and LVLM training. Both problems lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal gains and potentially misguide the study of LVLM.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: MMStar benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: Both problems lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal gains and potentially misguide the study of LVLM. To this end, we present MMStar , an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: In the future, we plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM's and LVLM's training corpora.
